newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-General sells Mauritania mine assets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-General sells Mauritania mine assets.

text.p: Australia-based General Gold Resources NL said on Tuesday it had signed a letter of agreement to sell its Mauritanian copper and gold mine assets to Canada's Solomon Resources Ltd in exchange for 25 million Solomon shares valued at C$1.40 each, or C$35 million.
Part of the transaction calls for Solomon to undertake an equity raising of C$10 million at a price not less than C$1.40 a share, General Gold said.
The Mauritanian assets include a 50 percent interest in the Guelb Mogrhein project, which contains an estimated 1.1 million ounces of gold and 452,000 tonnes of copper, with cobalt credits.
The potential for developing the project, estimated to cost about US$130 million is currently in the feasibility stage, General Gold said.
The study is scheduled to be completed later this month or in early April, a company spokesman said.
The other 50 percent in the project is held by Societe Arab des Mines de l'Inchiri (SAMIN), a consortium of the Mauritanian and several Arab governments.
General Gold said the deal provided greater confidence for its shareholders that the capital needs for development of the assets could be met.

"This deal will see the Mauritanian assets transferred to a specialist West African mining and exploration company which, critically, has access to North American capital markets and which has the capacity to raise the sort of capital required by the Guelb Moghrein project to ensure its successful development
and to fund General Gold's increased exploration activities in Mauritania," General Gold managing director Cliff Harding said.
Solomon Resources is associated with Canadian mining identities Ronald Netolitzky and Lawrence Nagy.

Solomon's key assets include exploration interests in Burkino Faso in West Africa, exploration properties in Alaska, and minor interests in several oil and gas production businesses in the United States, General Gold said.
The deal still requires shareholder and regulatory approvals, General Gold said.
